correctness.rationale: For 3 iid Haar normals, Girard's four sign-cone cell areas A_i=2πp_i are affine functions of pairwise angles α,β,γ with ∑p_i=1 and the claimed Jacobian 2π³. The known Gram density sinα sinβ sinγ/(4π√G), with G=4∏sin(πp_i), gives the symmetric p-simplex density. As p0=u→0 the rescaled density √u g tends pointwise to (π^{3/2}/4)√∏_{j=1}^3sin(πq_j) with an integrable common majorant, and integrating u^-1/2 gives a √ε marginal. Overlap of two tiny p_i contributes only O(ε² log1/ε), so the four disjoint leading faces multiply by 4. Replacing ε=x/(2π) yields P(M<x)∼√2 πJ√x, and conditioned p-min/ε→Beta(1/2,1) independently of the remaining ordered q's with tilted sine-product density. Independent 2D quadrature found J=0.21817592130673527 and coefficient 0.9693300782906765; finite simulation is only corroborative.

Its unusually heavy √x tail, explicit non-elementary constant and independently marked macroscopic complement provide a useful rare-geometry description; the conditional law is not a textbook marginal of the already known largest-cell result.
